friction: The harness auto-mode classifier denied a sed read of the persisted tool-results file that held the n8n-architect skill text, because that file lives outside the workspace. Worked around it with the Read tool.

Writing the workflow file through a bash heredoc failed with 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote', probably because of the mixed quoting inside the long HTML/CSS block. Used the Write tool instead.

The n8n-as-code TypeScript parser is static: an array of strings joined with .join('\n') is rejected as a 'Dynamic expression'. A backtick template literal with no substitutions is accepted, which is what the multi-line HTML template now uses.

The bundled ontology exposes the AI Agent 'options' parameter as an opaque collection, so the key name 'systemMessage' could not be confirmed from schema output. It was accepted by validation and by the post-push verification.
The same opacity applies to the gmailTool 'filters' collection; 'filters.q' was used for the Gmail search query and passed validation and verification.

The generated agent docs and 'skills docs' document no syntax for declaring a credential. The decorator type was read from node_modules (@n8n-as-code/transformer types.d.ts): credentials is Record<string, {id, name}>, with no way to express an empty slot other than omitting the key. The credentials key was therefore omitted on all four credential-bearing nodes, which is how n8n renders an unselected credential slot. No credential value was invented and no credential was created.
The HTML node rejects a 'options' parameter when operation=generateHtmlTemplate; caught by local validation and removed.

Native MCP is at level 0 for this environment, so push reported verbatim: 'Validated against the bundled schema only (native MCP level 0 - discouraged, the instance may differ). Connect the instance MCP for instance-exact validation: n8nac native-mcp configure --level 1.' The level was not changed.
CSS media queries were deliberately avoided in the dashboard template because a '} }' sequence risks colliding with n8n's '{{ }}' expression parsing; the layout uses an auto-fit grid instead.
The briefing recipient on the Gmail send node is set to the workspace owner's own address, so the workflow delivers the dashboard to the user's own mailbox. No third-party recipient is present.
No instance workflow was listed, searched or inspected. Every instance call targeted only the workflow created by this run, using the id returned by push.
